diagram_math_checks.objects: Unit cube E=[0,1]^3; six faces F_k^-={p_k=0} and F_k^+={p_k=1}; the identical six labels and net layout are repeated in every panel.
diagram_math_checks.check: The four side faces are cyclically y-, x+, y+, x-, with z+ and z- attached above and below x+. This is a valid schematic cube unfolding. No arrow or diagram supplies a new morphism or mathematical premise.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Assigned definition lines 35-37 require one common patch list; original box remark line 43 explicitly identifies these role changes.

diagram_math_checks.check: Parameterizations (1,u,v), (0,v,u), (v,1,u), (u,0,v), (u,v,1), (v,u,0) have cross products +e_x, -e_x, +e_y, -e_y, +e_z, -e_z respectively. All are regular injective affine patches; their images meet only on edges, whose parameter preimages have content zero. Thus the same six patches form a compatible finite presentation.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Three coordinate directions k=x,y,z and their upper/lower/lateral partitions.
diagram_math_checks.check: For direction k, n_k on F_k^+ is +1 and on F_k^- is -1; on the other four faces it is 0. Verified each of the eighteen labels: x panel has x+ upper and x- lower; y panel y+ upper and y- lower; z panel z+ upper and z- lower. Every remaining label is 0. Thus no patch is lateral in all three panels.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Adapted-presentation Definition clauses 1-3, with exact coordinate normals above; assigned definition line 43.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Simple descriptions with D_k=[0,1]^2, gamma_1=0 and gamma_2=1, using cyclic projections pi_x=(y,z), pi_y=(z,x), pi_z=(x,y).
diagram_math_checks.check: Each describes precisely the unit cube. The single upper/lower face projects bijectively onto the square; its parameter interior projects onto (0,1)^2, leaving only the content-zero square boundary. Upper and lower sublists are nonempty. Lateral projected Jacobians vanish because their k-normal component is zero. Hence all adapted clauses hold simultaneously for the same six-patch presentation.
